title: Underlying derived invariants comparison for finite-dimensional profinite representations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. Let $G$ be any profinite group. Put $A=\underline E$, $C(P)=\{f\in C(P,\Omega): f(P)\text{ lies in one finite subextension}\}$, $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, and $c:C\hookrightarrow B$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Use the action categories $\mathcal A_G(R)$ of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], their ordinary unbounded derived categories and the ordinary total right derived invariant-submodule functors $R\Gamma_G$ [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. For $R=C,B$, let
$$F_R(K)=\operatorname{ev}_*R\Gamma_G(R\otimes_A^L K),\qquad K\in D(\mathcal A_G(A)),$$
where $G$ acts trivially on $R$, diagonally on the tensor, and $\operatorname{ev}_*$ evaluates a condensed module at the one-point profinite set and forgets scalars. These are exact functors to $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. Scalar inclusion induces a natural transformation $\alpha:F_C\to F_B$ compatible with the exact functors' shift isomorphisms; it is induced on a K-flat model by $z\otimes v\mapsto c(z)\otimes v$ and on derived invariants by scalar restriction and the inclusion of invariant submodules.

For every finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $W$ with continuous $E$-linear $G$-action, put $\underline W(P)=C(P,W)$. Then the actual morphism
$$\alpha_{\underline W[0]}:\operatorname{ev}_*R\Gamma_G(C\otimes_A^L\underline W)\longrightarrow\operatorname{ev}_*R\Gamma_G(B\otimes_A^L\underline W)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. No internal condensed isomorphism is asserted before evaluation, and no finite cohomological dimension or finite generation of $G$ is required. In particular the claim does not identify these derived invariants with underived continuous cochain complexes for the incomplete norm field $\Omega$.

proof.text: Choose an $E$-basis of $W$ of size $d$. By [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous] its coordinates give $\underline W\cong A^d$. This degree-zero module is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]: tensor with it is a finite direct sum, preserving acyclicity. Thus $R\otimes_A^L\underline W=N_R=R^d$ with the given $E$-matrix action and entrywise coefficient inclusion, for $R=C,B$. When $d=0$ the assertion is the zero comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-subextension-derived-function-columns] at $P=G^n$. The normalized maps assemble over the group nerve: the first face uses the continuous matrix $\rho(g_1)$, the others precompose parameter maps. By [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] and [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison], the $C$-column isomorphisms yield a total isomorphism. Exact point evaluation [lem-zl-contractible-derived-sections-tensor], at $T=*$, preserves finite diagonals. We obtain the canonical isomorphism $j_C:Q(C^\bullet_{\mathrm{fin}}(G,V_\Omega))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{ev}_*R\Gamma_G(N_C[0])$. Here each cochain has image in one finite $F^d$, and its differential is the displayed inhomogeneous formula in the cochain lemma below.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-norm-algcl-evaluated-bar-augmentation] for the canonical isomorphism $j_B:Q(C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_\Omega))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{ev}_*R\Gamma_G(N_B[0])$. The coefficient square in [lem-sfb-finite-subextension-derived-function-columns] and scalar naturality of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] give $\alpha_{\underline W[0]}j_C=j_B Q(i)$, where $i$ is the literal cochain inclusion. In particular the square concerns the specified coefficient map, including its invariant augmentation. This uses the evaluated total augmentation for $B$, without asserting acyclicity of its individual columns.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-finite-subextension-continuous-cochain-quasi-isomorphism], $i$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes $Q(i)$ invertible. The square therefore gives $\alpha_{\underline W[0]}=j_B Q(i)j_C^{-1}$ invertible in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. The tensor and derived-invariant maps used throughout are the stipulated ones, so their given shift-compatible natural transformation is unchanged. No internal condensed isomorphism before evaluation is concluded.

(1) finite-subextension-derived-function-columns is true. A[P] = j_P!A_P is flat (03EV). For finite F the normed-scalar node, with its field renamed to F (a complete finite extension), gives the F columns. C^d is the sectionwise filtered colimit, which the filtered-colimit node commutes with H_P. The coefficient square holds by naturality, and no B-column invertibility is claimed. That is correct, since cech-exact(1) gives H^1(V,C(-,Ω)) ≠ 0. (2) continuous-cochain-quasi-isomorphism is old steps 5-7 (H^0, coordinatewise E-linear retraction, local descent plus transfer, m^-1 in E); I checked each input statement. (3) norm-algcl-evaluated-bar-augmentation is the B-side core. It is well formed and passes d=0, G=1 and finite G. Old step 2 had misquoted the finite-only normed-scalar node for Ω (C4); the worker reports this and replaces it with this node. It is not a restatement, because C, descent and α are carried by separate nodes. Old steps 1 and 8 and the C-half of step 4 are kept whole in the assembly. The Q58 ce5b RETURN counterexample (G=Z_ℓ, W=E) fails: its ψ is not a section of Ĉ/Ω over Z_ℓ. Take a nonprincipal ultrafilter of integers converging to x₁. The remaining case is a plausible Borel-rigidity question that stays the WANTED core.
